Repository state supplies ARMED_k and a CAS transition to LAUNCH_CLAIMED_k(owner_nonce) immediately before the external mutation. adversarial_trace.event: Actor A holds ARMED_k, wins CAS to LAUNCH_CLAIMED_k(owner_nonce=A), and exact-reads the durable claim before any external mutation.

History H0: A crashes after exact readback of LAUNCH_CLAIMED_k(A) but before the target mutation. History H1: A performs the target mutation and crashes before authoritative matching B(k) or C(k) becomes durable.
A restarted or overlapping actor sees the same repository state in H0 and H1: LAUNCH_CLAIMED_k(A). owner_nonce proves who won the repository claim, not whether the external mutation occurred.

Any repository-only reconstructor must choose the same action in both histories. Relaunch can recover liveness in H0 but may duplicate a committed non-idempotent effect in H1; blocking preserves safety in H1 but leaves H0 unresolved until authoritative B(k) or C(k), or target-side A/fencing, resolves the ambiguity.

bounded_leaf_result.first_counterexample: Adding LAUNCH_CLAIMED_k(owner_nonce) moves the indistinguishability window but does not eliminate it: a durable pre-mutation claim cannot encode the later external side effect across a crash. The nonce survives; launch occurrence does not.
